title: Whole-body 3D kinematics of freely behaving Drosophila
source_locator: Results 2.5; Fig. 5c-d; Methods (Fly husbandry and behavioral experiments); Supplementary Video 5 legend
quote: Illuminating the arena with a red LED reliably elicited sustained running bouts, which we tracked with a modified headless skeleton
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC/Namiki type name DNg100; the split-GAL4 VT058557-AD; R85F12-DBD is also listed in driver_lines.csv as DNg100 (BDN2).
stimulation: red LED flashlight (the arena's white strobe illumination may also activate CsChrimson); flies aged 14 d, all-trans retinal 1/250 for 1 day
sensory_condition: decapitated, freely moving in a 3D-printed glass-floored chamber (rainbow rig), recorded at 800 fps
coordination_notes: induced running kinematics fall within wild-type running PC space; reduced femur/tibia flexion
penetrance: red light 'reliably elicited sustained running bouts'
n_flies_note: n=50 running cycles analysed (speed matched); number of flies not stated
notes: Preceding sentence (text.txt, Results 2.5): 'We expressed CsChrimson in DNg100, a descending neuron previously identified as a command neuron sufficient to drive rhythmic running in headless flies'. Fig. 5c (figure: 'Optogenetically induced running (DNg100 activation)', L1 tarsus tip shows repeated steps after 'red light ON'). The Supplementary Video 5 legend says 'The fly speeds up when the red light turns on', so the fly may already have been moving: the white imaging strobe can itself activate CsChrimson (Discussion 3.3). Because of this, effect_on_walking = speeds and confidence = medium. Legs coded yes per the walking convention (running in a headless fly). Line specificity is not characterised in the paper; the kit lists no off-target cells. Surface: floor of free-walking chamber (headless_surface = other). Sex not stated for this experiment.
